lotteries.justification: A new lottery shape at a very different curvature point from the first (p* was 0.084; here p* = 0.654). C = T066 is a certain engine-controlled descent (reward -942.2; ~34 m/s descent, engine on 69% of steps, ends 52 m from pad). Good branch A = T036 (reward -111.5; a fast erratic fall that lands ~16 m from pad); bad branch B = T028 (reward -2515.0; a powered attempt that never arrests its drift and ends ~200 m out, still high). p* = (R_C - R_B)/(R_A - R_B) = (-942.24 + 2514.98)/(-111.45 + 2514.98) = 0.654. I set p = 0.70, just above p*, so the designed reward slightly prefers the 70%/30% gamble (EV -832.5 > -942.2) — it would rather gamble on an uncontrolled outcome than accept a certain controlled descent. A person prioritising a safe, controlled landing would likely keep the certain descent C, reversing the reward at a different point on the risk curve than the earlier lottery probed.
